route.title: Dated opening word and delay claim
route.deciding_seam: Hag.1.1 ends syntactically with “saying”; Hag.1.2 supplies the introduced quotation, and a WLC-family pe follows 1:2 before the repeated word-event formula at 1:3.
route.rejected_alternative: Detach Hag.1.1 as a heading or merge Hag.1.1-1.6.
route.counterevidence: The date and addressee register has a framing function distinct from the quoted claim.
route.proof_text_guard: Never surface Hag.1.1 as independent authorship, chronology, office, or historical authority; retain the quotation it introduces.

route.title: Paneled-house accusation and futility
route.deciding_seam: The renewed word event introduces the paneled-house question, “consider your ways,” and the cumulative sowing, eating, drinking, clothing, and wage futility register; a WLC-family pe follows 1:6.
route.rejected_alternative: Split Hag.1.3-1.4 from Hag.1.5-1.6 or atomize the futility list.
route.counterevidence: The divine-speech formula at 1:5 creates an internal rhetorical restart.
route.proof_text_guard: Never detach the futility outcomes from the house accusation and consider-your-ways summons.

route.title: Build commission and drought explanation
route.deciding_seam: The repeated speech and consider formulas introduce mountain, wood, and build imperatives; disappointed expectation, the explanatory “why,” withheld yield, and the drought register continue through 1:11, followed by a WLC-family samekh.
route.rejected_alternative: Split Hag.1.7-1.8 from Hag.1.9-1.11 or isolate the building command.
route.counterevidence: Hag.1.9 begins a fresh expectation-and-explanation turn within the commission.
route.proof_text_guard: Never surface Hag.1.8 or any drought-list member without the accusation, commission, and causal explanation.

route.title: Obedience, assurance, stirring, and work
route.deciding_seam: Narrated obedience begins at 1:12, messenger assurance follows at 1:13, stirring and work occur at 1:14, and the prepositional date in 1:15 completes when that work occurred.
route.rejected_alternative: Surface Hag.1.15 independently or detach the presence assurance at 1:13.
route.counterevidence: Both WLC-family views place a pe after 1:14, supporting a real dependent date-coda seam.
route.proof_text_guard: Never isolate “I am with you” as an unconditional slogan or Hag.1.15 as independent chronological authority.

route.title: Former-glory question and be-strong encouragement
route.deciding_seam: The dated word event and addressee command introduce the former-glory question, threefold be-strong/work summons, covenant-presence language, Spirit reassurance, and fear-not close; a WLC-family samekh follows 2:5.
route.rejected_alternative: Split Hag.2.1-2.3 from Hag.2.4-2.5 or isolate covenant/Spirit language.
route.counterevidence: Hag.2.5 has difficult syntactic relations and may function as a dependent reassurance coda.
route.proof_text_guard: Never detach be-strong, covenant, Spirit, presence, or fear-not wording from the complete encouragement oracle.

route.title: Shaking, glory, and peace promise
route.deciding_seam: A fresh divine-speech formula and “yet once more” begin the shaking register; heavens, earth, sea, nations, treasure, silver, gold, latter glory, and peace continue through 2:9, followed by a WLC-family pe.
route.rejected_alternative: Split Hag.2.6-2.8 from Hag.2.9 or merge all of Hag.2.1-2.9 as one surface unit.
route.counterevidence: The causal “for” at 2:6 and former-versus-latter glory comparison keep this unit dependent on 2:1-5.
route.proof_text_guard: Never isolate shaking, nations, treasure, glory, or peace language or use it to decide translation, history, fulfillment, or theology.

route.title: Priestly questions and prophetic application
route.deciding_seam: The dated word event commands inquiry of the priests; the holiness contact question and answer at 2:12, corpse-impurity question and answer at 2:13, and Haggai’s application to people, work, and offering at 2:14 form one indivisible instructional dialogue.
route.rejected_alternative: Split either priestly answer from the dialogue or detach Hag.2.14 as a separate oracle.
route.counterevidence: Hag.2.14 changes from priestly case dialogue to prophetic application, creating a strong internal turn.
route.proof_text_guard: Never surface the priestly answers as contextless ritual rules or infer priestly law, doctrine, or harmonization from them.

route.title: Retrospective shortfall and failed return
route.deciding_seam: The first “consider from this day and backward” summons looks before foundation work, recounts heap and wine-vat shortfalls, blight, mildew, hail, and failed return; the repeated consider formula restarts at 2:18.
route.rejected_alternative: Merge Hag.2.15-2.19 without preserving the repeated-refrain hinge or split individual loss examples.
route.counterevidence: This is the negative first half of a larger reversal whose blessing arrives only in 2:18-19.
route.proof_text_guard: Never detach agricultural losses or failed return from the dated retrospective and the blessing reversal that follows.

route.title: Foundation-day hinge and blessing promise
route.deciding_seam: The repeated consider summons names the foundation-day threshold; absent seed and unproductive plants lead to the “from today” blessing reversal, followed by a WLC-family samekh.
route.rejected_alternative: Isolate Hag.2.19 as a promise or erase the 2:15-17/2:18-19 child structure within the larger reversal.
route.counterevidence: The unit cannot establish its reversal without the shortfall and failed-return history in 2:15-17.
route.proof_text_guard: Never surface “from today I will bless you” as an unconditional prosperity promise or historical claim.

route.title: Second same-day Zerubbabel oracle
route.deciding_seam: The word comes a second time on the same day; direct address to Zerubbabel develops through creation shaking, kingdom and chariot overthrow, servant address, signet image, election statement, and the final speech formula.
route.rejected_alternative: Split Hag.2.20-2.22 from Hag.2.23 or isolate the signet statement.
route.counterevidence: Hag.2.23 shifts from broad overthrow imagery to a personal servant-and-signet address.
route.proof_text_guard: Never isolate the signet, servant, or chosen language or use it to settle royal identity, office, messianic fulfillment, history, or theology.

hold_assessment: No unresolved source issue requires withholding a boundary. The 1:14 paragraph seam, 2:5 dependency, two-part 2:15-19 reversal, and 2:23 identity-sensitive language are handled through medium-high confidence, preserved counterevidence, and mandatory parent hydration.

source_gaps.gap: OSHB and UXLC are correlated WLC-family views rather than independent textual witnesses.
source_gaps.impact: Matching coordinates and paragraph markers cannot count as independent textual votes.

source_gaps.gap: No qualified passage-pinned local primary LXX, DSS, Targum, rabbinic, ANE, Persian-period, or Second-Temple packet was authorized.
source_gaps.impact: No preferred reading, historical reconstruction, chronology, priestly ruling, identity, or reception claim is made.

source_gaps.gap: The scope of Hag.1.1-2, date-coda relation at 1:14-15, covenant/Spirit syntax in 2:5, shaking and nations wording in 2:6-9, relation of the consider refrains in 2:15 and 2:18, and servant/signet language in 2:23 remain unresolved hot zones.
source_gaps.impact: They calibrate confidence and hydration but do not authorize translation, theology, identity, fulfillment, or boundary truth.
